chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān said: It was narrated to me by Ishaq ibn 'Ammār from 'Umar ibn Yazīd who said: I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman
He said: She completes all the rituals, except that she does not perform tawaf between Ṣafā and Marwah

I said: For some of what she makes up from the rituals is greater than Ṣafā and Marwah, namely the standing at 'Arafāt; so why is it that she makes up the rituals but does not perform tawaf between Ṣafā and Marwah?
He said: Because Ṣafā and Marwah, she can perform tawaf upon them whenever she wishes, whereas these standing places (like 'Arafāt and Muzdalifah), she cannot make them up if they pass her by

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: Ṣafā and Marwah (the two hills between which tawaf is performed)

ai.seo_question: What rituals does a menstruating woman miss during 'Umrah and can she make them up?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of missed Hajj rituals for menstruating women, distinguishing between time-bound obligations like standing at 'Arafat and flexible ones like Sa'i. The Imam’s reasoning highlights the principle of 'qada' (making up) based on the nature of the ritual's temporal constraint, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility granted to women during their menses, ensuring they do not lose the validity of their Umrah despite missing specific components.
